title: What is the best year in film history?

commenti.body: 2023? It’s up there. Maybe too soon to say but it was truly a fantastic year for movies all around. The spectacle of Barbie/Oppenheimer, art house masterpieces in Anatomy of a Fall and The Zone of Interest. Poor Things too. And KOTFM, The Holdovers. The list goes on and on

2022? It's up there. Maybe too soon to say but it was truly a fantastic year for movies all around. The spectacle of TÁR/Syk pike, art house masterpieces in Unrest and Godland. Viking too. And Please Baby Please, Piaffe. The list goes on and on

To me, the issue with picking such a recent year is that none of its films have had time to become canonical, influence other filmmakers, etc.

We really don't know how people in 2040 or 2050 will perceive any of those films. 

Another issue is ticket sales: approximately 830 million (US), compared to 1.225 billion in 2019 and well over 1.5 billion in both 2002 and 2003.
[removed]
One issue would be that it's the third lowest-grossing cinematic year this century (after the two pandemic years). Its ticket sales were less than half of what they were in any year in the 2000s.

Some solid experimentation in both indies and mainstream films and a ton of classic “Oscar bait” films that have actually stood up to the test of time.

I think it has a strong case. 

Can you think of anything historically important to in terms of innovative technology or technique that was really popularized that year?
Don't forget Blair Witch Project which redefined the horror genre

Your comment on innovative technology made me think of The Phantom Menace also released in '99.


Not a great film especially in retrospect  and the CGI has its failures. But it definitely started the trend into the next millennium, for better or for worse.

Maybe the most over-hated film ever. 

If Blair Witch, another 1999 film, was the first film to use a viral marketing campaign online, then Episode I was the first film — and maybe the first big pop culture thing in general — to have an online hatedom.
And also helped redefine movie marketing.

To me 2019 was pretty strong. 
Portrait of a Lady on Fire, Parasite, Jojo Rabbit, The Irishman, Midsommar, The Lighthouse, Beanpole, Marriage Story, Les Misérables, Uncut Gems, Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, Ema, Us, The Wild Goose Lake, 1917, Pain and Glory. 

Oh, and Cats. Absolute cinema.
Its status as the last year of regular moviegoing pre-pandemic gives it a place in film history.
